# Staged LiteRT SDK

This directory is the repo-local staging area for the LiteRT runtime and GPU
accelerator shared libraries used by `libscyllasband`.

## Layout

```text
third_party/litert/
├── include/
│   └── litert/
│       ├── c/                  # Public C API headers (litert_compiled_model.h, ...)
│       │   └── options/        # Accelerator-specific options (CPU, GPU, ...)
│       └── build_common/
│           └── build_config.h  # Hand-written, matches the prebuilt flags
└── lib/
    ├── android-arm64/
    │   ├── libLiteRt.so
    │   └── libLiteRtClGlAccelerator.so
    ├── android-x86_64/
    │   ├── libLiteRt.so
    │   └── libLiteRtClGlAccelerator.so
    ├── linux-x86_64/
    │   ├── libLiteRt.so
    │   └── libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so
    ├── linux-arm64/
    │   ├── libLiteRt.so
    │   └── libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so
    ├── macos-arm64/
    │   ├── libLiteRt.dylib
    │   └── libLiteRtMetalAccelerator.dylib
    ├── ios-arm64/
    │   ├── libLiteRt.dylib
    │   └── libLiteRtMetalAccelerator.dylib
    ├── ios-sim-arm64/
    │   ├── libLiteRt.dylib
    │   └── libLiteRtMetalAccelerator.dylib
    └── windows-x86_64/
        ├── libLiteRt.dll
        └── libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.dll
```

The files under `lib/<platform>/` are gitignored local build artifacts.

## Policy

- The repo stages LiteRT public C headers from upstream `google-ai-edge/LiteRT`
  so `libscyllasband` builds against the real upstream C ABI.
- `build_config.h` is normally generated by CMake from `build_config.h.in`.
  Since we consume prebuilt shared libraries rather than building LiteRT
  ourselves, this repo keeps a hand-written stub matching the prebuilt flags.
- Keep the runtime and accelerator versions matched. If you download the GPU
  accelerator from Google's prebuilt table, download the matching runtime from
  the same LiteRT version.
- When bumping LiteRT, update both the headers in `include/litert/` and the
  shared libraries in your local staging directory.

## Stage From The Python Wheel

The historical path still stages the runtime library from an installed
`ai_edge_litert` wheel for the current host platform:

```bash
python scripts/stage_litert_sdk.py --overwrite
```

## Stage Official Runtime And GPU Prebuilts

For native GPU acceleration, stage both the runtime and the separate GPU
accelerator library. The helper downloads the published prebuilt for the current
host platform by default:

```bash
python scripts/stage_litert_sdk.py --download-runtime --download-gpu-accelerator --overwrite
```

Use `--platform` for packaging another supported desktop, Android, or Apple mobile target:

```bash
python scripts/stage_litert_sdk.py --platform linux-x86_64 --download-runtime --download-gpu-accelerator --overwrite
```

Supported platform names are `android-arm64`, `android-x86_64`,
`linux-x86_64`, `linux-arm64`, `macos-arm64`, `ios-arm64`,
`ios-sim-arm64`, and `windows-x86_64`.

## Stage Local Downloads

If the matching shared libraries already exist on disk, copy them into the
repo-local staging directory:

```bash
python scripts/stage_litert_sdk.py --source-lib /path/to/libLiteRt.so --source-gpu-accelerator-lib /path/to/libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so --overwrite
```

After staging, rerun CMake with `-DSCYLLASBAND_ENABLE_LITERT=ON` and rebuild the
native targets.

For standalone Linux GPU/WebGPU diagnostics that were not built with the
repo-local RPATH, export the staged library directory before launching native
tools:

```bash
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$PWD/third_party/litert/lib/linux-x86_64:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
```

This is needed because LiteRT's accelerator registry dynamically loads GPU
plugins such as `libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so` by library name.
